Article Title: Isro’s GSLV-F17 successfully places EOS-05 Earth observation satellite in geosynchronous orbit
Article Text:
ISRO’s GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission successfully accomplished

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRIHARIKOTA: The Indian Space Research Organisation ( Isro ) successfully launched EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite designed to operate from a geosynchronous orbit, aboard GSLV-F17 in the early hours of Friday.The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at Sriharikota at 2.55am and placed the around 2,367kg Earth observation satellite in its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.This was the 19th GSLV flight. GSLV-F17 had a S139 solid core with four L40H liquid strap-ons, a GL40HT liquid second stage and a CUS15 indigenous cryogenic upper stage, besides a four-metre composite ogive payload fairing.EOS-05 was injected into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a nominal perigee of 171km, apogee of 31026km and inclination of 19.28 degrees. The satellite will be moved to the final orbit through a series of manoeuvres using onboard thrusters.Isro chairman V Narayanan said the rocket injected the satellite in the intended orbit precisely. This is the 107th launch from Sriharikota and 19th GSLV flight. The chairman addressed from the mission control complex post launch."From launching 1536kg payload in the first GSLV launch, the chairman said the rocket has carried the heaviest payload in its history at 2367kg. We gradually improved the performance of the vehicle by optimising the structural mass and improving propulsion system. The satellite is India's first dedicating imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit. It will provide strategic data."The chairman also said Isro will have six more launches this financial year including navigation satellite NVS-03 and Gaganyaan first uncrewed mission.India had 21 operational Earth observation satellites as of February 2026. Of these, most are in low-Earth or sun-synchronous polar orbits, while India’s geostationary-orbit Earth observation capability is currently represented by the meteorological satellites INSAT-3D, INSAT-3DR and INSAT-3DS. EOS-05 is India’s first imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit.The launch was the first GSLV mission since GSLV-F16 successfully placed the joint Nasa-Isro NISAR Earth observation satellite in a 743km sun-synchronous orbit on July 30, 2025. Friday’s launch was Isro’s second orbital mission of 2026. The first, PSLV-C62 carrying EOS-N1 and other payloads on Jan 12, failed following an anomaly towards the end of the rocket’s third-stage flight.
Article Summary: Isro’s gslv-f17/eos-05 mission successfully accomplished on friday. The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at sriharikota at 2.55am. The satellite is india's first dedicating imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit.

Article Title: Punjab government to hike DA of 85,000 employees from 42 to 60 pc: Minister Aman Arora
Article Text:
Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chandigarh, Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday.Speaking to mediapersons here, Arora said a recommendation in this regard was made by the Cabinet Sub-Committee formed to examine the issues of employees.The announcement is significant as employees recruited after July 17, 2020 were getting a pay equivalent to the Central pay scales, along with 42 per cent Dearness Allowance (DA). These were much lower than the pay scales of employees recruited before July 2020, who were paid as per the Punjab Pay Commission.Arora said there were two pay scales in Punjab, which was leading to conflicting interests and confusion: the Punjab basic pay scales and the one equivalent to the Central basic pay scales (as per the 7th Central Pay Commission)."Punjab basic pay scales, which traditionally are higher, range from 30 to 70 per cent more than the Central basic pay. And when DA is added to it, which is currently 42 per cent, the salary increases much above the Central pay scales," he said."When we calculate and compare, even with 60 per cent DA added to Central basic pay, the Punjab pay scales and take-home salaries are higher," he said.Arora said the previous Congress government had decided to hire employees on the Central pay scales after July 17, 2020.In the last six years, 85,000 employees have been recruited.The Mann government will give them a "Janmashtami gift" as the three-member Cabinet Sub-Committee has decided that the DA of these employees will be raised from 42 to 60 per cent. The committee's recommendation will be sent to the chief minister, Arora said.He, however, said that this hike will not benefit employees recruited before July 2020."From day one, the Bhagwant Mann government has been talking about the welfare of every section. We cannot imagine good governance without our employees," he said.The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including the release of their pending 18 per cent DA.They have also threatened to go on mass casual leave on September 8 if the state government does not withdraw a recent notice imposing disciplinary action against those who remained on "unauthorised absence" on August 27.The employees have given the state government time till September 7 to withdraw the notice issued to protesting employees.Punjab government on Thursday appealed to employee unions to engage with it through dialogue rather than confrontation, calling employees the backbone of good governance.
Article Summary: Punjab government will raise the dearness allowance of around 85,000 government employees by 18 per cent to 60 per cent. The announcement is significant as employees recruited after july 17, 2020 were getting a pay equivalent to the central pay scales. The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike.

Article Title: 'Outstanding achievement': PM Modi hails Isro after successful EOS-05 launch
Article Text:
The Prime Minister also highlighted the expanding role of Indian industry in the country's space programme. He said the growing partnership with ISRO was helping strengthen the sector and broaden India's capabilities.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday lauded the Indian Space Research Organisation ISRO ) after the successful launch of the GSLV-F17 rocket carrying the advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05), calling the mission an “outstanding achievement” and a proud moment for the nation.The satellite was launched by Isro from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday aboard the GSLV-F17. The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg EOS-05 into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit (Sub-GTO), marking another major milestone for India’s space programme.“Yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation. The successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit is a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector," PM Modi said in a post on X.The Prime Minister also highlighted the expanding role of Indian industry in the country's space programme. He said the growing partnership with ISRO was helping strengthen the sector and broaden India's capabilities."The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem," he added.Isro chief V Narayanan described the mission as a significant achievement for India's space programme. He said the satellite was in good health after being injected into orbit.“I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite 05, the geo-imaging satellite, in the intended and required orbit," he said.Narayanan said EOS-05 would become India's first dedicated imaging satellite operating from a geosynchronous orbit once it is operationalised. The satellite is expected to provide important strategic data for the country.“Today, we have injected the heaviest satellite, 2367 kgs, using this launch vehicle. The health of the satellite is perfectly alright,” the ISRO chief said.The GSLV-F17 mission was the 19th flight of India's geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle. It was launched from the second launch pad at Sriharikota and carried EOS-05 towards a sub-GTO.The mission adds to India's growing earth observation capabilities while highlighting the increasing technological strength of its space programme.
Article Summary: The satellite was launched by isro from the satish dhawan space centre in sriharikota on friday aboard the gslv-f17. The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg eos-05 into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit (sub-gto)

Article Title: Cruise tourism gets a boost as govt clears e-group visa
Article Text:
The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As the govt focuses on positioning India as a leading global cruise destination, the home ministry has introduced e-group visit visa (cruise) for foreign tourists arriving in India on cruise vessels which follow a fixed and predetermined itinerary.The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The latter will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. The e-group visit visa (cruise) will have a validity of 30 days and allow multiple entry.The cruise operator or agent of the vessel will need to submit the application for e-group visit visa for international passengers via the specified portal or mobile app, three days before berthing of the vessel at the first Indian port. No fresh application will be accepted beyond this cut-off.There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e-group visit visa (cruise), home ministry sources told TOI. The details of the foreign passengers — name, nationality, passport number and issue/expiry date, etc — can be uploaded in bulk on the specified portal ( indianvisaonline.gov ) or mobile app.The e-group visit visa shall contain a QR code. Passengers may use this QR code at immigration checkpoints at the port of entry and for further travel within India, as per the fixed cruise itinerary.“Easier visa and immigration procedures will encourage international cruise companies to include Indian ports in their itineraries. This will also generate wider economic benefits for ports, hotels, restaurants, transport operators, touring businesses and local communities,” said an MHA official.The govt has, since 2024, launched two major initiatives to boost cruise tourism in India, given the great potential that the country’s 7,500-km coastline and a network of 110 navigable waterways connecting 400 rivers, presents, as per a PIB statement issued in April last year. The first initiative is Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024 with the aim of doubling the cruise traffic in India by 2029 (from 4.7 lakh in 2024 to almost 10 lakh in 2029). Also, the Maritime India Vision 2030 aims to make the country a significant player in the global cruise market, covering oceanic and coastal cruises, island and infrastructure development and river and inland cruises.
Article Summary: The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The latter will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter india from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry make major $5.6 million move for underprivileged Oakland children ahead of the new season
Article Text:
Stephen Curry raises funds.(Image via Getty Images)

Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry make a multi million dollar move for their foundation

Stephen Curry weighs in on the impact created by their foundation as he gears up to make a comeback

Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ legend, might be preparing for the new season but both he and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have remained devoted in their philanthropic activities. While the two have raised a lot of funds for their foundation, Eat, Play & learn, the high profile couple have made another multi million dollar move.A few hours ago, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play recently took to its social media to make a post that read as, “The seventh annual Workday Charity Classic was one for the books! An incredible day, all in support of @eatlearnplay. Grateful to @workday, co-founder Aneel Bhusri, and everyone who came out.”The post added, “Thanks in part to a generous match from Aneel, this year’s event raised more than $5.6 million with funds going straight toward Eat. Learn. Play.’s mission: helping a generation of Oakland students access nutritious food, quality reading resources, and opportunities to play and be active. Thank you to everyone who made this event a success and for standing with us in support of Oakland students.”This was not the first time that the high profile couple have raised millions to help underprivileged children and families in Oakland.For close to a decade, both Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have raised over $100 million funds which have gone directly to the community they have been able to build back in their hometown in Oakland.The two have been able to build schools, playgrounds and provide meals to children coming from underprivileged backgrounds in Oakland.A few days ago, at the annual golf tournament hosted by Workday, Stephen Curry opened up about their foundation’s impact in Oakland as he said, “The clarity around how, you know, our impact would show up around the play yard builds, library renovations, those type of things, that's been the biggest, I guess, reward that we've had because we understand…”The four time NBA champion added, “Ayesha has a, a great story she tells about a kid that, when she got to en- enjoy or see, the unveiling of one of our first playground builds, it was a surprise to her that that was for her and her classmates and her students, so like, or her friends, as a place that was, you know, built and, and dreamed of for them.”Ahead of the new season, the focus remains on the legend Stephen Curry as he spends his time in recovery while preparing to return to court.
Article Summary: Stephen curry and his wife, ayesha curry, have raised over $100 million for their foundation, eat, learn & play. The two have been able to build schools, playgrounds and provide meals to children coming from underprivileged backgrounds in oakland.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5 million nonprofit faces scrutiny after records show $469,000 spent on management and $446,000 on charity
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce nonprofit spending comes under scrutiny

Travis Kelce foundation says tax filings were incorrect

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis Kelce ’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations.In January, 2026, according to federal tax records examined by The Arizona Republic, Eighty-Seven and Running reported about $1.5 million in revenue during the three-year period and roughly $1.1 million in expenses. About $446,000 was listed under charitable spending, while $469,000 was reported as management costs.That works out to about 41 cents of every dollar spent going toward charity based on the filings. Charity Navigator generally views nonprofits spending at least 70 cents of each dollar on programs as efficient, while CharityWatch uses 75 cents as a benchmark for high efficiency.The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group.The company was co-founded by Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes. Aaron Eanes also serves as the nonprofit’s executive director.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, raised concerns about the structure after reviewing the records.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” said Laurie Styron, the executive director of CharityWatch, an independent charity watchdog group that reviewed the nonprofit’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic.“That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”..Travis Kelce’s team disputes the picture presented by the filings. Aaron Eanes said the reported figures did not properly classify some operational expenses tied to charitable work.“Operational costs for charitable efforts were “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services,” Eanes told The Republic, so the public records do not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed.”.Eanes said the foundation has since changed its approach, adding that management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025. He also said the organization plans to expand its board, bring in nonprofit advisers and improve its reporting practices.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards.”The scrutiny comes as the NFL continues to highlight charitable work through the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program. Kelce has been nominated three times and has supported causes in both Kansas City and his hometown of Cleveland.Kelce's foundation’s reported numbers do not erase that community work, but they do highlight why financial transparency matters. For celebrity-led nonprofits, public trust depends not only on how much money is raised, but also on how clearly and responsibly that money reaches the people it is meant to help.The foundation has since said it took steps to address the accounting and governance concerns, including changing how expenses were reported and eliminating management fees in 2025. However, there has been no public indication that the concerns raised by CharityWatch and The Arizona Republic have been formally cleared or independently resolved
Article Summary: Travis kelce’s eighty-seven and running foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other nfl-linked organizations. The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to a&a management group.

Article Title: Did Clay Matthews get plastic surgery? ‘Unrecognizable’ photos spark controversy over former NFL star’s dramatic appearance
Article Text:
What happened to Clay Matthews? New photos spark plastic surgery rumors; here’s what we know

Clay Matthews plastic surgery rumors grow after alleged photos

Clay Matthews’ recent podcast appearances raise more questions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former NFL linebacker Clay Matthews is facing plastic surgery rumors after photos shared online appeared to show him looking very different. However, there is no confirmed evidence that Matthews underwent cosmetic surgery, and the images themselves have been questioned. An X community note attached to the post claims the pictures were AI-generated and falsely show Matthews after cosmetic work. The original post also carried an “#ad” tag, although it is not clear what the advertisement was promoting. Matthews, meanwhile, appeared in recent podcasts looking like himself, adding more doubt to the claims surrounding the photos.The photos showed Clay Matthews apparently shopping for groceries, with his face looking noticeably different from the former Green Bay Packers star’s usual appearance. They were shared by TMZ on social media, rather than in a separate report on its website.That quickly led to speculation that Matthews may have had plastic surgery. But the pictures have not been established as genuine photographs of a recent change in his appearance.An X community note attached to the post says: “The post uses AI-generated images falsely depicting Clay Matthews after cosmetic work. No credible sources report any such change.”That does not, by itself, prove that the images were created with AI. Still, it gives an important reason not to treat the plastic-surgery claim as fact. The “#ad” label also raises questions about the purpose of the post. There has been no clear explanation of what the advertisement was for.The unusual images also led to comments from people who believed Matthews had changed his appearance. One person wrote, “Clay Matthews got reconstructive surgery to look like the gigachad meme 😭,” while another said, “You won’t believe how much he spent just to look this.” A third person added, “This can’t be real,” showing that some viewers were already questioning whether the pictures were genuine.The timing of the photos is another reason the claim needs caution. Matthews appeared on The Ryen Russillo Show on September 3, just before the images circulated. The episode featured him discussing his work with Netflix, the Rams-49ers game in Australia and his life after football.Matthews also appeared on Bussin’ With The Boys on September 3 alongside Will Compton, Taylor Lewan and Delanie Walker. The episode focused on the 2026 NFL season and included Matthews discussing the league and making predictions for the year.Those appearances make the sudden change shown in the alleged photos harder to accept as proof of surgery. They do not establish what the images are, but they do show why the claim remains unconfirmed.Matthews is also returning to the NFL spotlight this season through Netflix. The streaming service announced that the six-time Pro Bowl linebacker would join Michael Irvin and Nick Foles as part of the studio team for the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia.For now, there is no reliable confirmation that Clay Matthews had plastic surgery. The photos remain disputed, while the X community note and the “#ad” label leave open the possibility that they were created or used for promotional purposes.Clay Matthews is facing plastic surgery rumors after unusual photos appeared online. However, the images have not been confirmed as genuine, and an X community note claims they were AI-generated. The post also carried an “#ad” label. Matthews appeared in recent podcasts looking familiar, so there is currently no reliable evidence that he underwent cosmetic surgery.
Article Summary: Clay matthews is facing plastic surgery rumors after unusual photos appeared online. However, the images have not been confirmed as genuine, and an x community note claims they were ai-generated. Matthews appeared in recent podcasts looking familiar, so there is currently no reliable evidence that he underwent cosmetic surgery.

Article Title: ‘Floor-collected, broken noodles used to make bhujia': What FSSAI found at Wai-Wai's Rajasthan unit
Article Text:
India's food regulator FSSAI has ordered CG Foods India to stop producing veg bhujia





NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has directed CG Foods India Pvt Ltd to stop production of its ‘Veg Bhujia Namkeen’ after an inspection at the company’s facility in Rajasthan found multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The food regulator said on Thursday that enforcement action had been initiated against the company over “unsafe processing, unlicensed bhujia manufacturing, and predated packaging”.During an inspection at the company’s unit in Roopangarh, Ajmer, officials found floor-collected and broken noodles being reprocessed into bhujia without heat treatment, FSSAI said.The inspection also uncovered the use of predated packaging and the unlicensed manufacture of ‘Wai-Wai MaMa’ and ‘Wai-Wai Mama Punte’ bhujia variants, allegedly in violation of Section 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said officials seized 32,107.2 kg of stock, including loose broken noodles, from the premises.The inspection further revealed deficiencies in hygiene and documentation, including inadequate pest-control records and other food safety lapses.Officials collected samples for laboratory testing and detained 1,925 boxes of expired finished products. Legal proceedings have also been initiated against the company.FSSAI directed CG Foods India to discontinue production of Veg Bhujia Namkeen products without the required approvals and corrective measures.The regulator said further action would be taken based on the laboratory test results and findings of the inspection.
Article Summary: India's food regulator fssai has ordered cg foods india to stop producing veg bhujia. During an inspection at the company’s unit in roopangarh, ajmer, officials found floor-collected and broken noodles. Legal proceedings have also been initiated against the company.

Article Title: Meta's highest-paid employee Alexandr Wang can't stop making fun of Google, says who is ...
Article Text:
Meta AI head

The benchmark behind Alexandr Wang’s dig at Google

Where the gains came from

The cost advantage

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer and highest-paid employee recently took a jab at Google ’s Gemini after a benchmark data shoed Meta’s latest AU model climbing near the very top of the industry rankings. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Wang wrote, “I really hate to say it, but… gemini who? 🚀💨” alongside a performance chart showing Meta’s Muse Spark 1.3 surpassing several Gemini variants on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. According to Artificial Analysis, Muse Spark 1.3 scored 62 points, placing it behind only Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 (66) and Claude Opus 5 (63). The model outperformed Google’s Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash, which scored 61 and 53 respectively.Wang's comment was posted in response to a thread from Artificial Analysis announcing that Meta had released Muse Spark 1.3, the company's fourth Muse Spark model release in just five months. According to the benchmark firm, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) — currently in limited preview for Meta's partners — scored 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, trailing only Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5 in their top configurations.The publicly available variant, Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh), scored 61 on the same index, putting it in a tie with GPT-5.6 Sol (max), Grok 4.6 (high), and Claude Opus 5 (high). That score represents a 4-point jump from Muse Spark 1.2's score of 57 in August, and an 8-point gain over Muse Spark 1.1's score of 53 in July. It landed just behind Claude Fable 5.1 (max, 66), Claude Opus 5 (max, 63), and Claude Fable 5 (max, 62).According to Artificial Analysis, both new Muse Spark variants improved primarily in two areas: agentic task performance and scientific reasoning.On agentic work, Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh) posted a 12-point gain over Muse Spark 1.2 on the Tau3-Bench Banking evaluation, rising from 35% to 47%, along with a 5-point gain on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (80% to 85%) and a jump in GDPval-AA v2 Elo rating from 1,615 to 1,709. The limited-preview Muse Spark 1.3 (max) variant pushed even further, reaching 52% on Tau3-Bench Banking — the highest score of any model on that specific benchmark — and a GDPval-AA v2 Elo of 1,754. Artificial Analysis noted that Muse Spark 1.3 (max) achieves these higher scores in part by using significantly more reasoning tokens than the xhigh variant, reasoning 62% more on GDPval-AA v2 and 28% more on Tau3-Bench Banking.On scientific reasoning, the standout gain came on CritPt, where the xhigh variant improved 8 points over Muse Spark 1.2, from 18% to 26%. GPQA Diamond rose 4 points, from 90% to 94%, while Humanity's Last Exam and SciCode each posted more modest 2-to-3-point gains.Beyond performance, Muse Spark 1.3 also demonstrated efficiency. The xhigh variant costs about $0.55 per task, significantly lower than GPT‑5.6 Sol and Grok 4.6, which cost nearly double. Analysts noted this places Muse Spark on the “Pareto frontier” for intelligence versus cost, making it one of the most competitive models in terms of value.For those unaware, Meta has released four Muse Spark models in just five months, underscoring its aggressive push in frontier AI.

Article Title: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is launching a defense technology company backed by Palantir
Article Text:
Alex Karp backed defense company turning wartime experience into a product

A war reshaping military technology

Fedorov's abrupt exit from government

What Fedorov has been doing since leaving government

Palantir CEO Alex Karp stepping in as the first lead investor in a new defense technology company founded by former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedoro. According to a report by CNBC, the size of Karp’s investment has not been disclosed, but Fedorov’s press office confirmed the partnership, saying details of cooperation with Palantir will be announced gradually. In a video posted by Fedorov on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Karp praised the venture, saying it could bring Ukraine’s wartime knowledge and experience “as a product to allied countries.” He added: “You and your colleagues are launching a company that I think will be defining for the world.”The company’s name, specific technologies, and the extent of Karp’s involvement have not yet been disclosed. Palantir did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Fedorov’s office said the venture will build on lessons learned during Ukraine’s war with Russia, where drones, artificial intelligence, and battlefield software have played a critical role.The launch comes as Ukraine's ongoing war with Russia continues to accelerate the development and battlefield deployment of technologies including drones, artificial intelligence, and military software.Fedorov, long known as a vocal advocate for using technology to modernize Ukraine's military, said the new company would apply lessons learned during the war to build technology usable by both Ukraine and its allied partners.Fedorov, 35, said in a statement: “During the full-scale war, our team gained unique experience working with defense technologies in Ukraine and seeing firsthand how technology is transforming modern warfare.” He added that the company will aim to apply those lessons to products usable by both Ukraine and its allies.Fedorov, 35, was removed from his role as defense minister by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in July as part of a broader government reshuffle, after serving in the position for just six months. Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai sends a message to his college IIT Kharagpur as it celebrates 75 years; shares happy memories as student: Meals at Harry's, studying in…
Article Text:
Image credit: Instagram

Sundar Pichai's IIT Kharagpur memories: Harry's, Illu and room B-308

Pichai's AI prediction: from labs to farmers, doctors and government offices

IIT Kharagpur at 75: why Pichai is betting on students

Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has recorded a video message for IIT Kharagpur as the institute turns 75, and he spends most of it on the small stuff. Meals at Harry's. The Illu festival. Nights spent studying in room B-308. The wingmates, and the professors who stuck with him. Campus, he said, is also where he met his wife Anjali, where he first learned to program, and where he carried floppy disks around to get time on one of the few machines available. "These moments shaped the course of my life," he said, "putting me on a path to Google."That last line is the pivot. The message, posted by IIT Kharagpur on X, works as two things at once—a nostalgia reel and a forecast. Pichai, who graduated in 1993 with a B.Tech in metallurgical engineering, uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years, and to make a case that universities, not just tech companies, will decide whether any of it reaches people who aren't already using it.The specificity is what makes it land. B-308 in Nehru Hall is an unremarkable hostel room—bed, study table, chair, almirah—and it has quietly become a campus landmark, currently occupied by a final-year chemical engineering student.Metallurgy, meanwhile, sits nowhere near the top of India's engineering pecking order, which is part of why the room has the pull it does.Pichai called an education from the institute "truly a gift" and said IIT Kharagpur "played a formative role in shaping the lens through which I strive to make an impact on the world." He also noted how far its graduates have travelled, in India and outside it.The forward-looking half is the newsier one. "When I look at the next five years, I see AI moving away from the lab and the early adopters and into the hands of people doing the work," Pichai said—"the healthcare workers, the government officials, the farmers, developers, and entrepreneurs."The framing is deliberate. He is not describing AI as something to experiment with, but as something that sits inside jobs people already do. "We are building AI so that it can help all of us do our work at the next level and do it in a more fulfilling way," he added.It also tracks with where Alphabet has pointed itself. Under Pichai, AI now runs through Search, Cloud and the Gemini family of models a shift the company's own regulatory filings describe as central to its strategy. A prediction about AI spreading into everyday work is, conveniently, also a description of Google's product roadmap.On India, Pichai said the country is increasingly producing innovations that can benefit the whole world, and that an "ambitious, optimistic new generation of Indians" has the chance to reimagine what's possible. AI can amplify that potential, he argued, but universities are what keep it useful to everyone rather than to a narrow few—a point that doubles as the institute's brief for its next 25 years.Much of the current momentum, he said, is coming from students. He recalled meeting Gemini Student Ambassadors from across India at the AI Impact Summit in Delhi this year: "Their enthusiasm for how technology can improve lives was palpable, and it's why I'm so optimistic about the future." The role of IIT Kharagpur, he added, "will only grow in importance as you lead the next wave of technology."The institute responded by calling the message a reflection of "the enduring global impact of the IIT ecosystem," saying it now looks ahead "to nurture ideas, inspire generations and create solutions that make a difference to India and the world."After Kharagpur, Pichai went to Stanford and then Wharton. He joined Google in 2004, worked on Toolbar and Chrome before taking charge of product and engineering across its major platforms, became CEO in 2015, and added Alphabet in December 2019.
Article Summary: Google ceo sundar pichai has recorded a video message for iit kharagpur as the institute turns 75. He uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years. He says universities, not just tech companies, will decide whether any of it reaches people who aren't already using it.

Article Title: Amazon to hire 160,000 temporary workers this festive season

Ahead of the upcoming festive season, Amazon India has announced that it has created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across its pan India operations network that supports its ecommerce and quick commerce business. As we focus on building one of India’s largest, safest, fastest and most reliable operations network, we are also committed to building an inclusive workforce, with opportunities for thousands of women associates and persons with disabilities. This expanded workforce will help us strengthen our fulfillment and logistics capabilities and ensure we can handle the festive season seamlessly. Many of these associates continue their journey with Amazon beyond the festive period, while several others return year after year to work with us,” said Abhinav Singh, VP, Operations, Amazon India, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkiye.Amazon India claims to have fulfilment centers spread across 15 states, offering over 43 million cubic feet of storage space for seller inventory; sortation centers in 19 states; along with a network of close to 2,000 Amazon-operated and partner delivery stations. Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I knew that if I failed I wouldn’t regret that, but…” - a lesson about risk, failure and regret
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I knew that if I failed I wouldn’t regret that, but I knew the one thing I might regret is not trying.”

What Jeff Bezos meant by the quote

The modest beginnings behind a much bigger company

The long-term view behind a risky choice

Why failure mattered less to him than uncertainty

A lesson about decisions rather than ambition

Trying can be smaller than people think

Lessons to learn from Jeff Bezos’ quote

Failure is not always the worst outcome

Consider the cost of inaction

Think beyond the present moment

Regret can be a useful decision-making tool

Trying does not always mean taking a huge risk

Do not confuse uncertainty with failure

Security has a cost too

A decision does not need a guaranteed outcome to be worthwhile

Learn to separate fear from judgement

The goal is not to avoid every mistake

There are decisions that become difficult precisely because both choices carry a cost. Staying where things are familiar can offer security, while taking a chance can leave a person facing an outcome that cannot be predicted. Jeff Bezos encountered that dilemma in the 1990s, when he was working at the investment firm D. E. Shaw began considering an idea built around the rapidly expanding internet. Leaving a well-paid job for an online bookseller was hardly a guaranteed route to success. Bezos knew the business could fail. What mattered to him was a different possibility: that years later, he might look back and wish he had given the idea a chance. He eventually left his job and founded Amazon . The decision became one of the defining moments of his career, but the reasoning behind it came before anyone knew how the company would turn out.Bezos was describing the way he weighed the risk of leaving his established career. He did not know whether Amazon would succeed. In fact, he considered failure a realistic possibility.His thinking centred on regret rather than prediction. He imagined himself much older and considered how he might view the decision with the benefit of hindsight.If the business failed, he would at least know that he had attempted it. If he stayed in his job and never tried, there would be no answer to the question of what might have happened.The quote is therefore not simply about being unafraid of failure. It is about recognising that inaction can also have consequences. Sometimes the safest decision in the short term can leave a person with a longer-lasting question.It is easy to view the original Amazon through the scale of the company that exists today. That can distort what Bezos was actually deciding in 1994.Amazon did not begin as a plan to create a vast technology and retail company. It began as an online bookstore. The first version of the business was focused on selling books through a website at a time when buying something online was still unfamiliar to most people.The company opened its virtual doors in July 1995.Within its first weeks, Amazon had shipped books across the United States and to customers overseas. The catalogue also gave the business an advantage that physical shops struggled to match. It could offer a huge range of titles without having to keep every book on shelves.The early success did not prove that Bezos had known what would happen. It showed what happened after he decided to try.The phrase most closely associated with Bezos's decision is his “regret minimisation framework”.Rather than trying to predict every detail of the future, he imagined reaching old age and looking back at the choice. From that imagined future perspective, he considered which decision was more likely to cause regret. The framework simplified the problem. If Amazon failed, Bezos could return to the job market and continue with his career. If he never tried, he might spend years wondering whether the business could have worked.It was not a mathematical formula. It was a way of changing the time frame of the decision. A difficult choice in the present can look different when viewed from decades later.Failure produces an answer. If a business closes, a person knows that a particular approach did not work. If an application is rejected, there is a definite outcome. Even an unsuccessful project can reveal what needs to change.Not trying provides none of that. The possibility remains hypothetical. There is no evidence showing whether the idea could have succeeded or failed.For Bezos, that unresolved possibility was harder to accept than failure itself. That is perhaps the most precise way to understand the quote. He was not claiming that failure feels good. He was saying that failure was an outcome he could live with, while never making the attempt might leave a question that could not be settled.The quote can be applied without turning every difficult choice into an entrepreneurial gamble. A person considering a career change, a new qualification, a business idea or a creative project might ask a similar question: which outcome would be harder to live with years from now?Sometimes the responsible decision is to stay put. Financial obligations, family circumstances, timing and the consequences of failure all matter. Bezos's framework cannot account for every situation.What it can do is introduce another consideration into the decision, the cost of never finding out.There is also no need for “trying” to involve quitting a job or risking a life's savings.It might mean testing an idea on a small scale. Applying for an opportunity. Taking a course. Speaking to someone in an industry you are considering. Building a first version of a project before deciding whether to pursue it seriously.Those steps can reduce uncertainty without requiring an immediate leap. In that sense, the useful part of Bezos's thinking is not necessarily the size of the risk he took. It is the way he separated the fear of failure from the question of future regret.
Article Summary: Jeff bezos said he would not regret leaving his job to start amazon. He did not know whether the company would succeed. He considered failure a realistic possibility. He imagined himself much older and how he might view the decision with the benefit of hindsight. There is no evidence showing whether the idea could have succeeded or failed.

Article Title: Apple follows Google Maps, renames Lake Ontario to Lake America; US President calls change of names 'complete, ratified, and binding'

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics.
